claims.text: The initial metal or alloy is prone to oxidation in high-temperature oxidizing environments.
A DFT-based computational approach can model the formation and stability of passivating oxide layers.
DFT-based modeling can identify alloy compositions that enhance oxidation resistance.
DFT-based modeling can identify processing conditions that enhance oxidation resistance.
DFT-based potentials can be used to simulate oxidation kinetics.
DFT-based potentials can be used to simulate the formation of protective oxide layers.
Simulation-guided changes in composition or processing can promote formation of a stable protective oxide layer.
DFT simulations can characterize the stability of an evolving oxide scale.
A well-formed passivating oxide layer acts as a barrier to further oxygen diffusion.
Restricting further oxygen diffusion slows the overall oxidation rate.
Simulation-optimized alloy composition and processing conditions will produce a more stable oxide layer than the untreated control.
A more stable oxide layer will improve oxidation resistance relative to the untreated control.
The untreated material forms a less controlled or less stable oxide layer.
The less controlled or less stable oxide layer of the untreated material leads to higher oxidation rates.
Instability of the oxide phase can prevent formation of a consistent protective layer.
Thermal cycling or mechanical stress can disrupt formation or retention of a consistent protective oxide layer.
DFT predictions may differ from experimental oxidation behavior under complex real-world conditions.
